body: `AssetResolver` is the host-injected interface viewers use whenever a markdown body references a sibling file — `![alt](./diagram.png)`, ` ```csv src=./data.csv `, and future patterns (linked `.md`, embedded `.svg`). Viewers never know whether they're in Chrome, VS Code, or a web demo; they just call `assets.resolve(relPath)` and get back a URL they can assign to `` or pass to `fetch()`. **Interface** (defined in `@filemark/core`): ```ts export interface AssetResolver { resolve(relativePath: string, baseUrl?: string): Promise; } ``` Returns a URL string — either a `blob:` (for locally-read bytes) or a remote `https:` / `file:` URL. Callers must not assume either form. **Four implementations — picked by file ingest kind:** | Host context | Implementation | `resolve()` does | |---|---|---| | FSA folder (`kind: "fsa"`) | `FSAAssetResolver` | walks the `FileSystemDirectoryHandle` by path segments (`./img/foo.png` → `img/` sub-handle → `foo.png` file-handle → `File` → `URL.createObjectURL`). Caches blob URLs per (dir-handle, path). | | Drop-folder (`kind: "drop"`) | `DropAssetResolver` | looks up an in-memory `Map` populated at drop time from `items[].webkitGetAsEntry()` recursion. Returns `URL.createObjectURL(file)`. | | `file://` intercept | `PassthroughResolver` | returns `new URL(relativePath, sourceUrl).toString()` — the browser fetches via `file://`, which **works for images but not for CSV reads** (same-origin rules on file://). Datagrid `src=` refuses to fetch and renders a warning. | | Remote (`raw.github*`, etc.) | `PassthroughResolver` | same — `new URL(relativePath, sourceUrl)`. Works for CSV fetch if the host permission covers the origin. | **Lifecycle of a blob URL:** - Created on first `resolve()` call; cached per viewer-instance until tab close. - Revoked when the owning tab unmounts (tab close or viewer swap). Avoids leaking object URLs across long sessions. - `FSAAssetResolver` re-reads on handle-permission change (FSA handles can go stale if the folder is ejected and re-granted). **Datagrid-specific handling of `src=`:** 1. `opts.src` present → call `assets.resolve(opts.src, sourceUrl)`. 2. If resolver throws `ENOENT`-ish (file missing or handle gone) → render an inline error card, not an empty grid. Rule 3 — skeletons must warn. 3. If resolver is `undefined` (single-file ingest has no siblings) → same error card with "open as folder to use `src=`" hint. 4. On success → `fetch(url).then(r => r.text())` → Papaparse → DataGrid. 5. No retry, no auto-reload. Re-render on file change is a stretch-goal tied to auto-refresh (§14). **Security note:** the resolver is same-origin by convention. It MUST refuse paths that escape the root (e.g. `../../..`). `FSAAssetResolver` gets this for free (relative segments are walked against the directory handle; `..` either fails or stays within the granted root). Passthrough resolvers must `new URL()`-normalize and reject protocols other than the one of `baseUrl`.
